title: Serial overhead around seeding and setup
body:
On a 481.8 s search of all Pfam against one MGnify recall shard of 2,455,940 targets at 48 threads, the `-s` runtime tree shows 30 s of serial work, 6.2% of the run. Two items make up 72% of it, and both have known fixes:

| item | seconds | issue |
|---|---|---|
| mmseqs target db write | 15.5 | nail-fc2ac4 |
| profile parse in `build_pipeline` | 6.2 | nail-65ce8f |

The rest of the serial work sums to 1.7% of the run. The tree and the breakdown are in the notes. nail-7ea5c0 decided that moving nail's io onto `libsail` is separate work, now nail-167dd7, and neither fix waits on it.

## Out of scope

- Caching the target db across runs. It helps only repeated runs, and those do not matter here.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/415c993d
notes.text:
Serial time on the 481.8 s run:

| item | seconds | share of run |
|---|---|---|
| db write | 15.5 | 3.2% |
| pipeline build | 6.2 | 1.3% |
| slice, decide and merge | 3.4 | 0.7% |
| query and target index | 2.7 | 0.6% |
| seed index | 1.6 | 0.3% |
| convertalis | 0.7 | 0.1% |
| all serial | 30.1 | 6.2% |

Removing every item entirely would buy 6%. Below the two large items, the 2026-09-28 code survey found these mechanisms:

- `PrefilterDb` in `mmseqs.rs` reopens its file on every `get` and `next_n`. Its `from_path` validates every record with an open, a seek and a one-byte read. It scans for newlines by hand, and all of it runs on one thread between align calls. A held handle or a map, `memchr`, and rayon over queries would speed up slice, decide and merge together, worth about 3 s.
- The slice writes a record for `Terminated` queries too, per the TODO in `seed_stage.rs`.
- `Seeds::from_path` allocates a `String` and a `Vec` per TSV line, on one thread.
- The index passes run on one thread, because `from_path` hard-codes `CHUNKS=1`. The HMM index does a `strum` match per line, and nail then reads the HMM file a second time to parse profiles. One pass that indexes and parses would remove the second read.
- nail could read the per-iteration align dbs into `Seeds` directly and drop `convertalis` and the merge. That gains about 1 s and costs a parser for mmseqs's alignment record. These numbers do not justify it.

For proportion, the prefilter takes 225 s, 47% of the run, all inside mmseqs. The alignment stage at 93% busy idles about 12 s.
